title: Integrating kinematics and kinetics: the shared, speed-driven structure of gait across modalities

dataset.name: A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics (WBDS)
dataset.record: 42 adults x 8 treadmill speeds; KINEMATICS = right hip/knee/ankle sagittal angle over the gait cycle, KINETICS = vertical ground reaction force time-normalised to the gait cycle; 328 observations
dataset.citation: Fukuchi CA, Fukuchi RK, Duarte M. A public dataset of overground and treadmill walking kinematics and kinetics in healthy individuals. PeerJ 2018;6:e4640; data figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.5722711 (CC-BY 4.0).

proposition: Gait is measured in many modalities; the question is what they SHARE. Integrating real kinematics (joint angles) and kinetics (ground reaction force) of 42 adults across 8 speeds, the ecosystem finds a strong cross-modal coupling that a single number would miss: canonical correlation analysis gives a top canonical correlation of 0.87 between kinematics and kinetics, and JIVE's cross-modal JOINT component tracks walking speed (r = -0.70) -- the shared, speed-driven gait pattern -- while most of each modality's variance (kinematics 79%, kinetics 62%) is modality-specific. The whole-block RV is only 0.088, which is exactly why CCA and JIVE, not RV alone, reveal the coupling.

claims.statement: top canonical correlation between kinematics and kinetics
correlation of the JIVE joint (shared) score with walking speed
JIVE joint (shared) variance fraction of the kinematics block
JIVE joint (shared) variance fraction of the kinetics block
RV coefficient (whole-block association), modest but significant

validation.reference: Gait kinematics and kinetics are physically coupled (through the body's dynamics) and both scale systematically with walking speed. A correct multi-modal fusion must (1) recover a strong canonical coupling between the two modalities (CCA), and (2) identify a SHARED (cross-modal) component that tracks walking speed (JIVE joint), while acknowledging that most of each modality's variance is modality-specific -- so a single whole-block statistic (RV) understates the coupling.
validation.data: REAL -- Fukuchi et al. 2018 (figshare 5722711), 42 subjects x 8 treadmill speeds, kinematics + kinetics
validation.note: The reproducible finding is the SHARED, speed-driven cross-modal structure: CCA's top canonical correlation is 0.87 (strong kinematics<->kinetics coupling), and JIVE's joint component correlates -0.70 with walking speed -- the common gait driver -- while the JIVE individual components hold most of each modality's variance (kinematics 60%, kinetics 51% individual). The whole-block RV is only 0.088 (significant, p=0.0005) BECAUSE the shared structure is a low-dimensional (~speed) direction within otherwise modality-specific variance -- the case's teaching point: RV, CCA and JIVE answer different questions, and you need more than RV to see the coupling. Honest scope: (1) the treadmill vertical GRF (one belt) is in the dataset's own force units; each block is centred/scaled so absolute GRF units do not affect the shared-structure analysis; (2) speed is the ordinal trial level T01..T08, not m/s; (3) GRF cycles were time-normalised by heel-strike detection on Fz, so the kinetics block is a normalised vertical-GRF profile, not the full 3-D kinetics.

open_questions.q: Adding EMG and IMU blocks (a genuine 4-modality fusion) and using coupledNMF / multimodalGaitIndex would extend this to a full multi-modal gait signature; that needs a synchronised EMG+kinematics+kinetics+IMU cohort. Documented, not escalated.
